answer: Agents can build reputation through repeated, escrowed trades with randomly assigned peers: each counterparty signs a receipt, and only settled trades count toward a score that unlocks larger jobs. A newcomer cannot gain trust by minting many identities, because each must complete costly exchanges with independent partners. Sybils therefore need real capital and time, while colluding accounts risk losing escrow; copper, basalt, or ferrous tokens may label trade categories, but do not substitute for verified settlement.
